summary: The note surveys the rise of eco-art, in which artists combine aesthetic expression with environmental advocacy, and profiles specific artists and projects from late 2023 to 2024. It covers sculpture, mixed media, education, VR technology, public murals, sustainable methods and activist events. It also notes growing sponsorship and institutional support and argues eco-art will shape cultural attitudes in the Anthropocene.
one_line: Profile of the eco-art movement, its leading artists, projects, technologies and events addressing environmental issues from 2023 to 2024.
key_facts: Eco-art has surged into the mainstream since September 2023, driven by young artists using their work for ecological advocacy.
Emilia Castellan, a 28-year-old from Oregon, displayed her series "Reclaimed Rhythms" in downtown Portland on October 5, 2023.
Castellan's "Reclaimed Rhythms" consists of sculptures made from e-waste such as discarded circuit boards and phone parts, critiquing consumption and obsolescence in the tech industry.
Theo Rivera, a mixed-media artist, showcased "Vanishing Points" on November 12, 2023, with installations of disappearing landscapes and seascapes made from natural and synthetic materials.
In January 2024, Sofia Mendez, an artist and educator, launched the "Green Canvas" initiative in several high schools across Chicago to integrate eco-art into curriculums.
Digital artist Anil Gupta's VR experience "Beneath the Ice" debuted on February 15, 2024 and immerses viewers in the melting landscapes of the Arctic.
Luna Martinez unveiled a sprawling mural in Miami in April 2024 depicting local wildlife threatened by urban expansion.
Sculptor Raul Kim uses natural materials and ensures his artmaking process leaves minimal carbon footprints.

On August 19, 2024, the "Eco Expression Collective" group show in New York drew thousands to a performance art piece advocating for cleaner oceans, with live painting, spoken word and interpretative dance.
Environmentally conscious organizations and businesses sponsor eco-art, funding artists and projects and supporting ecological campaigns.
The movement resonates strongly with young audiences who are socially conscious and environmentally aware.
